note: Ps68 great war-hymn/processional (corrected; longest in Bk II, God-act + imagery heavy). Human IB concentrated in the RESPONSES: enemies' HATE + the WICKED/REBELLIOUS x2/GUILTY; against them the righteous' fivefold joy (righteous+GLAD+EXULT+JUBILANT+JOY), repeated SING/SING-PRAISES/EXULT x2, and BLESS God x3 (Blessed v19, Bless v26, Blessed v35); the peoples who DELIGHT in war; the SINGERS in procession. God-qualifiers ~45 (arise/scatter/ride/father-fatherless/lead-out/ascend/bear-us-up/strike/rebuke + his name/holy/salvation x3/power x6/majesty/might/Awesome/strength). Smoke/wax/snow/chariots/princes/procession imagery + recipients (fatherless/widows/needy) = standalone. Every candidate roled.

dims.v: hate (sane - those who hate him flee)
paired with the wicked who perish (v2)

'Let God arise... let those who HATE (sane) him flee before him!' — the enmity that cannot stand when God rises; sane here the hatred of God's foes, which scatters like smoke at his coming (the qualifier arise) — malice routed by mere divine presence
wicked (rasha - so let the wicked perish)
paired with those who hate God (v1)

'as wax melts before fire, so let the WICKED (rasha) perish before God' — the godless dissolved at God's presence; rasha here the wicked whose end is to melt away like wax, set against the righteous who are glad (v3)
righteous (tsaddiq - the righteous shall be glad)
the fourfold joy: glad, exult, jubilant, joy

'But the RIGHTEOUS (tsaddiq) shall be glad; they shall exult before God; they shall be jubilant with joy!' — the fourfold gladness of the upright, over against the melting wicked; tsaddiq here the righteous whose response to God's rising is overflowing joy, heaped up in four verbs
be glad / rejoice (samach - shall be glad)
'the righteous shall be GLAD (samach)' — the first of the fourfold joy; samach the gladness of the upright before God, the opposite of the wicked's dissolving dread
exult / leap for joy (alats - they shall exult)
'they shall EXULT (alats) before God' — the second of the fourfold joy; alats the leaping exultation of the righteous in God's presence
be jubilant / rejoice (sus - they shall be jubilant)
'they shall be JUBILANT (sus) with joy!' — the third of the fourfold joy; sus the exuberant rejoicing that crowns the righteous' response to God's coming
the joy that fills the jubilation
'jubilant with JOY (simchah)!' — the fourth of the joy-cluster; simchah the gladness that saturates the righteous' rejoicing before God
sing (shir - sing to God, sing praises to his name)
paired with singing praises and exulting
to the God who rides through the deserts, father of the fatherless (v4-5)

'SING (shir) to God, sing praises to his name; lift up a song to him who rides through the deserts' — praise of the God who rides the heavens and cares for the helpless; shir here the summons to sing to the God whose name is the LORD, father of the fatherless (v5, the qualifiers) — worship of the mighty yet compassionate God
sing praises (zamar - sing praises to his name)
'sing PRAISES (zamar) to his name' — the sung worship directed to God's name; zamar here the music offered to the name of the God who rides in triumph
before God (whose name is the LORD)

'his name is the LORD; EXULT (alats) before him!' — jubilation before the God named YHWH; alats here the exulting that answers the revelation of God's name — joy in the presence of the covenant God who rides the heavens
rebellious / stubborn (sarar - the rebellious dwell in a parched land)
set against the solitary God settles and the prisoners he leads out (v6)

'but the REBELLIOUS (sarar) dwell in a parched land' — the defiant left in barren exile; sarar here the stubborn, contrasted with the lonely God gives a home and the prisoners he frees (v6) — rebellion's reward is a scorched, homeless waste
rebellious / stubborn (sarar - even among the rebellious, that God may dwell)
receive gifts (even they), that God may dwell
the rebellious among whom God nonetheless dwells

'you received gifts among men, even among the REBELLIOUS (sarar), that the LORD God may dwell there' — grace reaching even the defiant; sarar here the rebels among whom the ascended God chooses to dwell — the marvel that his victory-gifts extend even to former enemies
the Lord, who daily bears us up
grounded in God our salvation who bears us up
because God daily bears us up, the God of our salvation (v19)

'BLESSED (barak) be the Lord, who daily bears us up; God is our salvation' — blessing for God's day-by-day sustaining; barak here the worshippers' blessing of the God who carries them every day (the qualifier up) — the mighty warrior-God who is also the daily burden-bearer of his people
guilt / guilty ways (asham - who walks in his guilty ways)

'the hairy crown of him who walks in his GUILTY WAYS (asham)' — the enemy persisting in guilt, whose head God shatters; asham here the guilt of those who keep on in their sin, marked for judgment — the wicked's obstinacy meeting God's strike (the qualifier)
in front, musicians behind, maidens with tambourines
leads into the call to bless God (v26)

'the SINGERS (shir) in front, the musicians last, between them maidens playing tambourines' — the worshipping procession into the sanctuary; the singers leading the festal march of praise, human voices at the head of God's triumphal procession
bless (barak - Bless God in the great congregation)
the corporate blessing led by the singers
of the God who has worked/summoned his power for them (v28)

'BLESS (barak) God in the great congregation, the LORD, O you who are of Israel's fountain!' — the corporate summons to bless God; barak here the assembled people's blessing of the God whose power has worked for them (v28, the qualifier) — praise in the gathered congregation
delight / take pleasure (chaphets - who delight in war)

'scatter the peoples who DELIGHT (chaphets) in war' — the bloodlust of hostile nations; chaphets here the peoples who love war, whom God rebukes and scatters — a warlike relish that God's judgment ends, that kings may bring him tribute instead
sing (shir - sing to God, O kingdoms of the earth)
paired with singing praises to the Lord
to the God who rides the ancient heavens (v33)

'Sing (shir) to God, O kingdoms of the earth; sing praises to the Lord' — the summons to the nations to worship; shir here the call for all kingdoms to sing to the God who rides the ancient heavens and sends out his mighty voice (v33, the qualifiers) — universal praise of the sovereign God
sing praises (zamar - sing praises to the Lord)
'sing PRAISES (zamar) to the Lord' — the nations' sung worship of God; zamar here the praise the kingdoms of the earth are called to offer the God who rides the heavens
God, who gives power and strength to his people
the closing blessing, echoing v19 and v26
the God who gives power and strength to his people (v35)

'Awesome is God from his sanctuary... he is the one who gives power and strength to his people. BLESSED (barak) be God!' — the psalm's closing doxology; barak here the final blessing of the awesome God who strengthens his people (the qualifiers) — the war-hymn ending, as it recurs, in blessing
